headline: Parc Adfer carbon-capture retrofit wins planning approval on Deeside
summary: Flintshire County Council approved Enfinium's ~£200m post-combustion carbon-capture retrofit at the Parc Adfer energy-from-waste facility in North Wales, capturing close to a quarter of a million tonnes of CO2 a year for the HyNet network, despite objectors' doubts over the 95% capture-rate claim. Consent decision following the officers' recommendation-to-approve briefed on 2 Nov.
co2crc_note: UK EfW-CCS consenting progress feeding the HyNet cluster; peripheral to CO2CRC's geological-storage focus but a marker of capture-project permitting momentum.
extractor_note: £200m is the previously-announced project capex, not new money committed at approval. Planning consent is the new event. Date/detail from Google-Alerts sampler metadata; WebFetch blocked so unverified. Material new development vs the 30 Oct 'recommended for approval' item briefed 2 Nov.

headline: JERA takes equity stake in Oman's 44.01 to explore CO2-mineralisation storage
summary: Japan's largest power generator JERA announced an investment in 44.01, the Oman-founded company that permanently stores CO2 by mineralising it in peridotite rock (with pilots in Oman and the UAE, including with Holcim in Fujairah), extending JERA's CCS value-chain strategy beyond conventional geological storage into mineralisation.
co2crc_note: Japan is a key Australia CCS value-chain partner; a Japanese major diversifying into mineralisation storage is strategically relevant to Australia's storage-destination role and to mineralisation R&D interest.
extractor_note: Equity investment amount not disclosed. JERA release URL encodes 4 Nov JST and the Google-Alerts sampler timestamp (21:15:36Z, shared with another entry) appears to be a batch-capture time, so the Melbourne calendar date sits on the window boundary; WebFetch blocked so unverified. 44.01 confirmed as an Oman/UAE CO2-mineralisation firm via corroborating search (Holcim Fujairah pilot).
